equations.interpretation: Water sonication produces hydrogen and hydroxyl radicals inside collapsing bubbles.
In the aqueous branch the source proposes radical-mediated thiosulfate reduction producing sulfide, sulfate and water; the text calls both radicals reducing.
Isopropyl alcohol scavenges hydroxyl radicals by hydrogen abstraction, yielding a secondary alcohol-derived radical and water.
The alcohol-derived radical is proposed to reduce thiosulfate to sulfide, with sulfite and acetone among the written products.
Cadmium ions and sulfide ions form CdS.

proposed_mechanism.reaction_order: The source associates the aqueous reaction2 pathway with hexagonal CdS and the alcohol-containing reaction4 pathway with cubic CdS, through reaction5.
proposed_mechanism.qualitative_kinetics: Authors state hexagonal formation is faster, attributing this to the sulfur-producing routes; no time-resolved rate or conversion curve is supplied.
proposed_mechanism.caution: These equations describe a proposed chemical pathway, not additional charged materials, measured intermediates or separately performed synthesis recipes.

source_interpretation.title: Crystallite and particle sizes describe different measurements
source_interpretation.text: Sample A has a reported Scherrer crystallite size of 5.3 nm and a TEM particle size of about 8 nm; sample B has 3.5 nm and around 5 nm, respectively. The source initially calls these consistent and later notes the TEM values are slightly larger. No exact equivalence, combined average, confidence interval or numerical distribution width is inferred.

source_interpretation.title: Solvent effects and radical pathways are proposed
source_interpretation.text: The authors associate isopropyl alcohol with reduced aggregation and altered CdS phase selection, and propose different radical-mediated routes to sulfide from thiosulfate. The reaction equations and kinetic explanation are source interpretation. No measured radical concentration, intermediate yield or comparative rate constant is supplied.

Conical-flask capacity, cover design, sonication-bath make/model, actual delivered acoustic intensity, cooling-water flow/temperature, purge duration/flow, mixing, pH and reaction yield are unreported. Ar purging occurs before irradiation; a continuous Ar atmosphere during all seven hours is not asserted.
Precipitate collection method, wash volumes/cycle counts, vacuum level, product storage and exact physical aliquot identities across measurements are unreported.

Scherrer crystallite sizes (5.3 nm A, 3.5 nm B) and approximate TEM particle sizes (8 nm A, 5 nm B) are separate method-specific quantities. No uncertainty, numerical size-distribution width or statistical sample count is supplied.
XPS composition and purity are qualitative; spectra are explicitly not shown and no stoichiometric ratio or impurity limit is reported.

The source mechanism is proposed and includes literature-based radical chemistry; intermediates, rates and solution speciation are not measured. No model coordinates or current optical/electronic property measurements are supplied.
